title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MURRAY'S BAGPIPES
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Murray Kincaid, a propane delivery driver in Butte, Montana.
His grandpa's bagpipes sat in a closet for thirty years.
And for thirty years, Murray said, Someday.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SOMEDAY
segments.quote: Never put off till tomorrow what you can do the day after tomorrow just as well.
segments.author: Mark Twain
lines: At Thanksgiving, Grandma Peg, ninety years old, asked, When will I hear those pipes again?
Murray grinned and quoted Mark Twain:
Never put off till tomorrow what you can do the day after tomorrow just as well.
Grandma did not laugh. She said, I'm ninety, honey. I don't have a day after tomorrow.
That night he opened the case, and promised her the Saint Patrick's Day parade.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE GOOSE
segments.quote: There is no education like adversity.
segments.author: Benjamin Disraeli
lines: His first note sounded like somebody stepped on a goose.
The dog left the room. Then his wife Carol left the room.
Then he remembered Benjamin Disraeli, the British prime minister:
There is no education like adversity.
So he honked on a practice pipe in the garage every night.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE NEIGHBOR
segments.quote: You cannot shake hands with a clenched fist.
segments.author: Indira Gandhi
lines: One morning, his neighbor Mr. Novak pounded on the door. Your racket woke me up!
Murray's fists curled. Then he remembered Indira Gandhi, India's prime minister:
You cannot shake hands with a clenched fist.
He opened his hands and asked why. Mr. Novak works nights at the hospital.
So Murray practiced at lunch, in the empty propane yard.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE BAND
segments.quote: Discipline is the soul of an army.
segments.author: George Washington
lines: He joined the town pipe band, led by Agnes, a seventy-seven-year-old retired nurse.
He wanted to play songs. She made him play scales. For two months.
Above her door hung a line from George Washington:
Discipline is the soul of an army.
So Murray did his scales. Every day. Agnes called him Private Kincaid.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: FIVE BELOW
segments.quote: Example is the school of mankind, and they will learn at no other.
segments.author: Edmund Burke
lines: Parade day was five below zero. He wore long johns under his kilt.
Two blocks in, his pipes let out a squeal like a teakettle.
But Agnes marched on ahead, steady as a clock.
He remembered a line from Edmund Burke, an Irish writer:
Example is the school of mankind, and they will learn at no other.
So he laughed, took a breath, and kept marching.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: GRANDMA'S SONG
segments.quote: Musical training is a more potent instrument than any other, because rhythm and harmony find their way into the inward places of the soul.
segments.author: Plato
lines: At the corner sat Grandma Peg in a lawn chair, under three blankets.
Murray stopped and played Grandpa's favorite tune, just for her.
She cried. Mr. Novak was next to her, holding her cocoa.
Agnes said Plato knew it:
Musical training is a more potent instrument than any other, because rhythm and harmony find their way into the inward places of the soul.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Start now. Learn from the hard part. Open your hands. Practice. Follow good examples. Play for the people you love.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Start now. Learn from the hard part. Open your hands. Practice. Follow good examples. Play for the people you love.
I tried the bagpipes once. My cat still won't talk to me.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
